0|fb7275acd6fb988313dddd8d3d19efa70d9015ad|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"locking/lockdep: Iterate lock_classes directly when reading lockdep files
When dumping lock_classes information via /proc/lockdep
the lockdep lock as the lock hold time is indeterminate. Iterating
over all_lock_classes without holding lock can be dangerous as there
is a slight chance that it may branch off to other lists leading to
infinite loop or even access invalid memory if changes are made to
all_lock_classes list in parallel.
To avoid this problem
column2: iteration of lock classes is now done directly

column1: on the lock_classes array itself. The lock_classes_in_use bitmap is
checked to see if the lock class is being used. To avoid iterating
the full array all the times
column2: a new max_lock_class_idx value is added

column1: to track the maximum lock_class index that is currently being used.
We can theoretically take the lockdep lock for iterating all_lock_classes
when other lockdep files (lockdep_stats and lock_stat) are accessed as
the lock hold time will be shorter for them. For consistency
also modified to iterate the lock_classes array directly.
